items.grounds: Re-derived both ways. The shipped strongest_rejected_alternative declines the 42:1-4 continuation 'since the fresh divine-speech-frame formula at oshb:Isa.42.5 is the book's ordinary marker for a new unit, and a parashah PE mark closes the preceding span immediately before it, at oshb:Isa.42.4' -- two coordinate because-grounds, and no digit anywhere in the row for the typicality clause. Byte re-sweep with the object named (the koh-amar formula, skeleton tier, verse counts): 48 verses book-wide; within chs 41-43 exactly 4 (MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16), 0 in ch 41; all four divine-owned by their own bytes -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte), כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte), כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.43.14, tier: byte), כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.16, tier: byte) -- so the auditor's digit is exact, and it is the digit the book-order neighbor row already ships for the identical warrant. Mark inventory: MT 42:4 carries PE (type correct; single-witness disclosed in the row), but prophets-parashah is tier-3 weak corroboration and cannot stand as a because-ground. Tested against the row: the onset itself is sound -- the frame re-collates at byte tier in the cited verse and is tier-1 on its own -- so the refusal survives on the frame alone and the defect is confined to the warrant field; not load-bearing, so not high. One nuance the finding does not state: the staged universals checker does not lexicon 'ordinary', so this is a typicality-standard judgment rather than a mechanical gate failure; it still qualifies as a defective warrant because the identical claim carries the mandated sweep in the neighbor row and because the tier-3 mark is presented as a coordinate ground. Medium stands.

device_notes ships '(sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in ch 42; 2 verses, the kavod noun)'. Re-swept with the objects named (skeleton tier, verse counts): the tehillah noun stands in 3 verses of ch 42 (MT 42:8, 42:10, 42:12) -- exact; the kavod noun stands in 35 verses book-wide and in 2 verses of ch 42 (MT 42:8, 42:12), so '2 verses, the kavod noun' is true only under a ch-42 domain the citation does not state and false at the book-wide scope a bare sweep citation implies. Tested against the row: every field of the shipped row (boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, device_notes) was read for a glory-noun claim and none exists -- the praise-noun thread וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י (oshb:Isa.42.8, tier: byte) / תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10, tier: byte) / וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.12, tier: byte) is the only thread argued, while the glory tokens וּכְבוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.8, tier: byte) and כָּב֑וֹד (oshb:Isa.42.12, tier: byte) are argued in the book-order neighbor row, not here. The digit is an orphan and domainless; it backs nothing load-bearing (the close rests on the PE at oshb:Isa.42.9, in the inventory, plus the first-person to hymn-imperative shift at oshb:Isa.42.10). Medium stands: a defective digit claim, not alone load-bearing; either half of the proposed change cures it.

The row states the new-things/new-song forms share 'the root at stem level, the attested tokens themselves returning tier NONE'. Re-collated with the staged collator in both directions: חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.42.10, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.42.9 returns skeleton -- its consonants are a contiguous substring of וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ (oshb:Isa.42.9, tier: byte); the reverse, that new-things token against oshb:Isa.42.10, returns none; the full phrases שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.42.9 and וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד (oshb:Isa.42.9, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.42.10 both return none. The symmetric NONE claim is therefore byte-false in exactly one direction, as filed. Tested against the row: the cut does not move -- the row already dismisses this seam texture at skeleton tier ('a skeleton-tier cohesion driver is disclosed texture'), the PE at oshb:Isa.42.9 is in the inventory, and the form shift to the imperative hymn-call at oshb:Isa.42.10 carries the close. A wrong tier label is a byte-checkable claim under the tier-disclosure standard (same discipline as a digit), not a mere omission, so the medium band is right; not load-bearing, so not high. The proposed restatement (skeleton, direction named) is what the bytes return.

Same token pair, this row's own opening seam. device_notes: שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10, tier: byte) 'takes up' וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד (oshb:Isa.42.9, tier: byte) 'at stem level, the attested tokens themselves returning tier NONE'. Re-collated both ways with the staged collator: חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.42.10, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.42.9 = skeleton; וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ (oshb:Isa.42.9, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.42.10 = none; each three-token phrase against the other verse = none. The symmetric NONE label is false in one direction; the filed correction (skeleton, direction disclosed) is what the bytes return. Tested against the row: the summary 'None of the three rises above a skeleton- or stem-level thread' remains true after the correction; the PE at oshb:Isa.42.9 and the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.13 are both in the inventory under the claimed types; the tier-1 form shift from first-person divine speech to the plural imperative hymn-call carries the high confidence untouched. Medium stands: a byte-false tier label is a defective claim rather than a disclosure omission, and it is not load-bearing.

device_notes ships '(sweep: 2 verses, the kavod noun)' beside '(sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in ch 42)'. Re-swept with the object named (skeleton tier, verse counts): the kavod noun stands in 35 verses book-wide and in exactly 2 verses of ch 42 (MT 42:8, 42:12); the tehillah digit re-verifies exact at MT 42:8, 42:10, 42:12. The glory tokens the row cites are real at byte tier -- וּכְבוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.8, tier: byte) and כָּב֑וֹד (oshb:Isa.42.12, tier: byte) -- so the thread is genuine and the count is right for ch 42, but a sweep citation with no domain reads at book scope, where 2 is false against 35. Tested against the row: the domain is recoverable from the two cited refs and from the tehillah half, which is why this is not higher than filed; but the sanctioned shorthand is a claim about a sweep, and as written it is wrong. Not load-bearing: the high confidence rests on the tier-1 form shift at oshb:Isa.42.10 plus the inventoried PE at oshb:Isa.42.9 and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.13. Medium stands; the proposed domain phrase is the exact cure.

strongest_rejected_alternative refuses folding MT 42:17 forward 'because the parashah SAMEKH mark closes at oshb:Isa.42.17 rather than before it, and the idol-trusters named there are third-person objects ... not the deaf-and-blind addressees the imperative of oshb:Isa.42.18 opens with' -- the mark is the first of two coordinate because-grounds, as filed. Inventory: MT 42:17 = SAMEKH and MT 42:13 = SAMEKH (types correct, single-witness disclosed in the row). Prophets-parashah is tier-3 weak corroboration and may not serve as a ground for refusing a rival. Tested against the row: the second ground re-derives from bytes on its own -- oshb:Isa.42.17 is third-person throughout, נָסֹ֤גוּ אָחוֹר֙ יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ בֹ֔שֶׁת (oshb:Isa.42.17, tier: byte) with the participial subjects הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בַּפָּ֑סֶל (oshb:Isa.42.17, tier: byte) and הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לְמַסֵּכָ֖ה אַתֶּ֥ם אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ (oshb:Isa.42.17, tier: byte), rendered by the translation witness as those who will be turned back at web:Isa.42.17, while oshb:Isa.42.18 opens on plural imperatives with vocatives, הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים שְׁמָ֑עוּ וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים הַבִּ֥יטוּ לִרְאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.42.18, tier: byte), rendered “Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.” at web:Isa.42.18 -- so the refusal holds without the mark, and the row's own boundary_rationale already places the SAMEKH as what 'strengthens the seam', i.e. corroboration. The defect is confined to the ordering of the warrant field and is not load-bearing. Medium stands; the proposed reordering is the cure.

device_notes reads in full: 'The blind-guiding promise of web:Isa.42.16 anticipates the blind-servant address of web:Isa.42.18-Isa.42.19 in the following span; this row discloses the shared imagery as a cross-seam echo without merging the two spans, since the addressee and grammatical person both shift at web:Isa.42.18's imperative onset.' No Hebrew is spliced and no tier is named -- the finding's description is accurate. Re-collated: the device is real and gradable, עִוְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.42.16, tier: byte) returns accent_stripped against oshb:Isa.42.18, where וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.18, tier: byte) stands, continuing at עִוֵּר֙ (oshb:Isa.42.19, tier: byte); the reverse direction returns none, so the tier is accent_stripped in the 42:16-to-42:18 direction, and the book-order neighbor row discloses the same device with both splices and that tier named. Tested against the row: nothing the row asserts is false -- the echo exists, it straddles the close seam, it is disclosed, and the merge-refusal warrant re-derives from bytes (the plural imperatives הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים שְׁמָ֑עוּ וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים הַבִּ֥יטוּ לִרְאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.42.18, tier: byte) against the first-person divine speech of וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.42.16, tier: byte)); the boundary rests on that tier-1 shift plus the inventoried SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.17. Under the severity law this is the low band: no defective warrant, digit, or mark claim is present -- it is a mechanical disclosure shortfall (missing pointed splice and tier label on a true cross-seam disclosure) whose cure is a splice-and-label edit with no change to the argument. Downgrade medium to low; the proposed change is the right cure.
